title: The drought rolling/frozen window split (obs-2026-08-10-1) has held for six recorded nights without a single crossing, and GDACS's own datemodified field -- never read by this observatory -- shows the 'frozen' class is itself two different source behaviours
statement: obs-2026-08-10-1.json split GDACS's six OPEN drought episodes into two classes from two nights of evidence (2026-08-08, 2026-08-09) and named what would be needed before a sensor could be written without curve-fitting: 'a third night distinguishing which class new droughts fall into, and whether frozen episodes ever resume rolling.' Six nights now exist (2026-08-08, 09, 12, 13, 14, 15 -- the two missing dates, 08-10 and 08-11, are the anchor-deadlock outage documented in sensor-registry-stall.json, not a gap in this check). Across all six, the split has held exactly, and it is precise, not merely directional: the four rolling droughts (gdacs-dr-1018332, gdacs-dr-1018431, gdacs-dr-1027450, gdacs-dr-1027465) carry properties.todate equal to exactly run_date minus 2 calendar days on every single recorded night, including across the three real calendar days lost to the anchor-deadlock gap (todate read 2026-08-07 on 08-09's snapshot and 2026-08-10 on 08-12's snapshot -- advancing by exactly the three calendar days that actually elapsed between observations, not by one step per observation). Their properties.datemodified re-stamps within the same one-minute window, 05:57:06 through 05:57:27 UTC, on every recorded night including 08-12 after the three-day gap -- evidence of a fixed daily source-side job, independent of whether this observatory happened to be watching. The two frozen droughts (gdacs-dr-1017863, gdacs-dr-1018327) show properties.todate byte-identical across all six snapshots (2026-03-30 and 2026-04-20 respectively). No drought has crossed classes and no drought has newly entered either class -- the registry has held at exactly six drought futures, four rolling and two frozen, since before this observatory's first night. A further split, invisible to obs-2026-08-10-1, appears only by reading properties.datemodified, a field GDACS carries on every event but which practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS (severity, window, what, where; line 29) never reads or compares: gdacs-dr-1017863's datemodified is a different timestamp on every one of the six recorded nights (2026-08-08T17:35:17 through 2026-08-15T05:55:20) even though its todate never moves, while gdacs-dr-1018327's datemodified reads the identical value, 2026-05-21T13:07:09, in every single preserved snapshot -- three months before this observatory's first night and never touched since. Both futures show zero REVISED events in foreknown/registry.json since NOTARIZED on 2026-08-08 (history length 1 each), so the current registry cannot distinguish 'the source re-examined this record today and confirmed nothing tracked changed' from 'the source has not looked at this record since May.' A spot check against non-drought events in the same 2026-08-15 snapshot (gdacs-eq-1556215: datemodified 2026-08-06, nine days stale, sitting beside gdacs-eq-1557236's 2026-08-15 in the same feature list) confirms datemodified varies per event rather than being a whole-feed batch stamp, so it is read as a genuine per-record signal, not noise.
method: Extracted properties.todate and properties.datemodified for eventid in {1017863, 1018327, 1018332, 1018431, 1027450, 1027465} from every preserved foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json where <date> in (2026-08-08, 2026-08-09, 2026-08-12, 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, 2026-08-15) -- the complete set of GDACS snapshots this observatory has ever committed. Computed run_date minus todate per night for the rolling class to confirm the exact 2-day lag, including across the 08-09-to-08-12 gap. Cross-checked against foreknown/registry.json's window and history fields for the same six ids to confirm zero REVISED or class-crossing events. Spot-checked datemodified across the first fifteen features of the 2026-08-15 snapshot to rule out a feed-wide batch timestamp. Reproducible with: python3 -c "import json; [print(d, sorted((p['eventid'], p['todate'], p['datemodified']) for p in (f['properties'] for f in json.load(open(f'foreknown/snapshots/{d}/gdacs.json'))['features']) if p['eventtype']=='DR' and p['eventid'] in (1017863,1018327,1018332,1018431,1027450,1027465))) for d in ('2026-08-08','2026-08-09','2026-08-12','2026-08-13','2026-08-14','2026-08-15')]".

figures.frozen_class_datemodified_static_since: gdacs-dr-1018327: 2026-05-21T13:07:09, unchanged across all 6 preserved snapshots

worth_watching_because: obs-2026-08-10-1.json deliberately withheld a sensor because two nights could not distinguish a stable source property from an artefact of when the observatory happened to be looking. Six nights, including a three-day gap that the rolling class tracked through without a step change, now supply exactly the stability evidence that proposal asked for -- filed as sensor-drought-window-class-crossing.json below, watching for the crossing that has not yet happened rather than assuming it never will. The datemodified finding is a second, distinct thing: not a pattern in what this observatory already tracks, but a field it has never tracked at all, which turns out to separate two source behaviours (reconfirmed-unchanged vs untouched-for-months) that the current registry renders identical. Filed as sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json.
